title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Issuing the Implementation Measures of the People's Courts for the Provisions on the Recording and Accountability of Judicial Personnel Inquiring about Cases
keywords_en: Improper Inquiry into Cases by Personnel within Judicial Organs
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Notice on Issuing the Implementation Measures of the People's Courts for the Regulations on Recording and Accountability for Internal Judicial Personnel Inquiring into Cases

Fa Fa [2015] No. 11

The High People's Courts of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army; the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the High People's Court of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region:

The Implementation Measures of the People's Courts for the Regulations on Recording and Accountability for Internal Judicial Personnel Inquiring into Cases are hereby issued, effective from August 20, 2015. Please earnestly implement them, ensure the filing of implementation rules and the regular reporting of implementation status, and promptly report any issues found during implementation to the Supreme People's Court.

August 19, 2015

Implementation Measures of the People's Courts Implementing the Regulations on Recording and Accountability for Internal Judicial Personnel Inquiring into Cases

Article 1 These Measures are formulated to implement the Regulations on Recording and Accountability for Internal Judicial Personnel Inquiring into Cases issued by the Central Political and Legal Affairs Commission, to ensure fair and honest justice, and in light of the actual work of the people's courts.

Article 2 Where a people's court personnel member encounters a request from a case party or a related person to inquire into a case, make solicitations or intercede, or inquire about case details, such personnel member shall refuse the request.

Article 3 Where a people's court personnel member encounters a request from a case party or a related person made in person to transmit case materials not through proper channels, the personnel member shall inform the requesting party to submit the materials directly to the case-handling unit and the case-handling personnel, or to submit them through a proper channel such as the litigation service hall of the people's court.

With respect to case materials mailed by a case party or a related person through improper channels, the people's court personnel member who receives them shall, depending on the circumstances, return or destroy the materials, and shall not forward them to the case-handling unit or the case-handling personnel.

Article 4 Where a people's court personnel member encounters a request from a case party or a related person to inquire about the progress of a case, the personnel member shall inform the requesting party to inquire directly with the case-handling unit and the case-handling personnel, or to make inquiries through proper channels such as the judicial information disclosure platform or the litigation service platform of the people's court. If a case party or a related person reports that an inquiry or search yielded no results, the personnel member may suggest that the party or related person file a complaint with the supervision department of the people's court.

Article 5 Where a people's court personnel member needs to inquire into a case, or to approve or transmit case materials in the performance of statutory duties, such action shall be taken in accordance with statutory procedures or relevant work procedures, and shall be fully documented and permanently preserved.

Unless in the performance of statutory duties or through statutory procedures or relevant work procedures, a people's court personnel member shall not inquire of a case-handling unit or case-handling personnel about a pending case, and shall not approve or transmit case materials to a case-handling unit or case-handling personnel.

Article 6 Where a leading cadre of a people's court or a personnel member of a higher-level people's court needs to provide supervision or guidance opinions on a pending case in the performance of statutory duties, such opinions shall be provided in writing in accordance with statutory procedures or relevant work procedures. If provided orally, the case-handling personnel shall truthfully record them and place them on file.

Article 7 The case-handling personnel of the people's court shall place in the case file for future reference the directives, correspondence, records, and other materials provided by a leading cadre of the people's court or a personnel member of a higher-level people's court in the performance of statutory duties for the purpose of providing supervision or guidance opinions.

Article 8 Where personnel members of other judicial organs need to learn about relevant circumstances of a case being handled by a people's court in the performance of statutory duties, the case-handling personnel of the people's court shall request that the other party produce legal documents or official letters and other supporting documents, record the contact details on file, and place them in the case file for future reference. If the other party fails to produce such documents, the case-handling personnel may refuse to provide the information.

Article 9 The people's court shall establish a dedicated database for information on internal judicial personnel inquiring into cases within the case information management system, and shall clarify the responsibilities, authorities, and work procedures for entering, storing, reporting, viewing, and processing relevant information. The supervision department of the people's court shall be responsible for the maintenance and management of the dedicated database.

Article 10 When, in the course of case handling, a case-handling personnel member of the people's court encounters a situation where an internal judicial personnel member inquires into a case outside statutory procedures or relevant work procedures, the case-handling personnel member shall promptly and fully and truthfully enter into the dedicated database for information on internal judicial personnel inquiring into cases the inquirer's name, unit, position, and the details of the inquiry, and shall retain relevant materials to ensure that there is a basis for verification.

Article 11 The supervision department of the people's court shall conduct a quarterly summary and analysis of the content entered into the dedicated database for information on internal judicial personnel inquiring into cases. If clues of problems involving internal judicial personnel inquiring into cases in violation of regulations are discovered, they shall be handled in the following manner:

(1) If the clues involve a subject under the jurisdiction of the supervision department of the court itself, the supervision department of that court shall directly investigate and handle the matter;

(2) If the clues involve a subject under the jurisdiction of the supervision department of a higher-level people's court, they shall be directly reported to the supervision department of the higher-level people's court with jurisdiction for investigation and handling;

(3) If the clues involve a subject under the jurisdiction of the supervision department of a lower-level people's court, they may be transferred level by level to the supervision department of the people's court with jurisdiction for investigation and handling, or may be directly investigated and handled by the supervision department that discovered the clues;

(4) If the clues involve personnel of other judicial organs, they shall be directly transferred to the discipline inspection and supervision department of the judicial organ where the personnel are located for investigation and handling.

Upon receiving clues transferred by the discipline inspection and supervision department of another people's court or another judicial organ, the discipline inspection and supervision department of the people's court shall promptly investigate and handle the matter and shall notify the discipline inspection and supervision department that transferred the clues of the results of the investigation and handling.

Article 12 Where a people's court personnel member commits any of the following acts, such acts shall constitute an act of inquiring into a case in violation of regulations, and the personnel member shall be given disciplinary sanctions in accordance with Article 33 of the Regulations on Sanctions for People's Court Personnel. If the act is suspected of constituting a crime, the matter shall be transferred to judicial authorities for handling:

(1) Interceding, inquiring about case details, or tipping off for a case party or a related person;

(2) Inviting case-handling personnel to meet privately with a case party or a related person;

(3) Approving or transmitting case materials to a case party or a related person not in accordance with proper procedures;

(4) Inquiring into a pending case of another person not in the performance of duties or not through proper procedures;

(5) Other acts of inquiring into a case in violation of regulations.

Article 13 After obtaining the approval of the principal leader of the court, the supervision department of the people's court may circulate within the people's court information on cases where the court or its subordinate courts have sanctioned people's court personnel for inquiring into cases in violation of regulations, and may also disclose such information to the public when necessary.

Article 14 Where a case-handling personnel member of the people's court commits any of the following acts, such acts shall constitute acts of violating case-handling discipline. If it is a first occurrence, a warning or a criticism notice shall be issued. If it occurs two or more times, disciplinary sanctions shall be given in accordance with Article 54 of the Regulations on Sanctions for People's Court Personnel:

(1) Failing to record, or failing to truthfully record, supervision or guidance opinions raised orally by a leading cadre of the people's court or a personnel member of a higher-level people's court;

(2) Failing to place in the case file for future reference the directives, correspondence, records, and other materials containing supervision or guidance opinions raised by a leading cadre of the people's court or a personnel member of a higher-level people's court;

(3) Failing to record, or failing to truthfully record, the contact details when personnel of other judicial organs seek information about a case, or failing to place the records and supporting documents such as legal documents and official letters of contact in the case file;

(4) Failing to enter into the dedicated database, or failing to truthfully enter into the dedicated database, information regarding internal judicial personnel inquiring into a case outside statutory procedures or relevant work procedures.

Article 15 Where the supervision department of the people's court fails to promptly handle or investigate clues regarding internal judicial personnel inquiring into cases in accordance with regulations, the supervision department of the higher-level people's court shall give disciplinary sanctions in accordance with Article 69 of the Regulations on Sanctions for People's Court Personnel. If the act is suspected of constituting a crime, the matter shall be transferred to judicial authorities for handling.

Article 16 Where a leading cadre of the people's court instigates the supervision department of the people's court not to transfer or not to investigate clues regarding internal judicial personnel inquiring into cases in violation of regulations, or instigates subordinates not to record, file, or enter in the database information on internal judicial personnel inquiring into cases in violation of regulations in accordance with regulations, disciplinary sanctions shall be given in accordance with Articles 69 and 76 of the Regulations on Sanctions for People's Court Personnel, respectively.

Article 17 The act of a case-handling personnel member of the people's court truthfully recording information about internal judicial personnel inquiring into a case is protected by law and the organization.

Unless for statutory reasons and through statutory procedures, a case-handling personnel member of the people's court shall not be dismissed, transferred, discharged, or given sanctions such as demotion, removal from office, or expulsion.

Article 18 Where a people's court personnel member retaliates against or engages in acts such as insulting, assaulting, or falsely accusing a case-handling personnel member who truthfully records information about internal judicial personnel inquiring into a case, disciplinary sanctions shall be given in accordance with Articles 70 and 98 of the Regulations on Sanctions for People's Court Personnel, respectively. If the act is suspected of constituting a crime, the matter shall be transferred to judicial authorities for handling.

Article 19 The performance of these Measures by people's court personnel members shall be incorporated into the evaluation and assessment system and shall serve as an important basis for assessing whether they comply with the law, handle matters according to law, are honest and self-disciplined, and for selecting them for awards, honors, or promotions.

Article 20 Where, due to inadequate supervision and punishment, acts of people's court personnel inquiring into cases in violation of regulations occur repeatedly within the scope of duties, the principal responsibility for the construction of party conduct and integrity of the unit leader and the supervisory responsibility of the discipline inspection and supervision department shall be pursued.

Article 21 Where a party member or cadre of the people's court violates these Measures and also violates the Regulations on Disciplinary Sanctions of the Communist Party of China, corresponding party discipline sanctions shall be imposed in addition to administrative sanctions.

Article 22 The term "case party or related person" as used in these Measures refers to a case party or the party's defender, agent ad litem, close relative, or any other person who has an interest in the case or the case party. The term "leading cadre of the people's court" as used in these Measures refers to leading cadres at the deputy director level or above in internal organs of people's courts at all levels and their directly subordinate units. The term "people's court personnel" as used in these Measures refers to personnel on the establishment of the people's court. The term "case-handling personnel of the people's court" as used in these Measures refers to the president, vice presidents, members of the adjudication committee, division chiefs, deputy division chiefs, members of collegial panels, sole judges, trial support personnel, and other personnel who participate in case handling, evaluation, review, and deliberation.

Where retired or departed personnel of the people's court, people's jurors, or employed personnel violate these Measures, they shall be dealt with by reference to these Measures.

Article 23 These Measures shall be interpreted by the Supreme People's Court.

Article 24 These Measures shall take effect on August 20, 2015. The Several Provisions on Preventing Court Internal Personnel from Interfering with Case Handling in Trial Work previously issued by the Supreme People's Court shall be abolished simultaneously.
